subject: Recap: Migration off proprietary LLM APIs — discovery & next steps
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: James Li <james.li@saasco.com>, Claire Nguyen <claire.nguyen@saasco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 16:32:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Today’s discovery — migration off OpenAI/Anthropic

Thanks again for taking the time today — good conversation. Below is a concise recap (pain, current stack, success criteria) and proposed immediate next steps so we’re aligned. Please call out any corrections.

Quick summary of what we heard
- Pain points:
  - API spend with OpenAI is the largest line item for your chat/assist flows (~$0.09/token effective after ops); aggressive cost pressure from leadership.
  - Vendor lock-in risk: model features (function-calling, streaming) differ between providers and some internal middleware tightly couples to OpenAI call shape.
  - Latency spikes on peak traffic causing poor UX outside P95 targets.
  - Data residency & auditability: security/compliance team needs VPC-hosted inference and audit logs for model access.

- Current stack (from today’s call):
  - Frontend calls -> internal proxy -> mixes OpenAI (chat + embeddings) and Anthropic (safety checks).
  - Monthly token volume: ~10M tokens (chat + embeddings).
  - Primary models: OpenAI gpt-4o-ish for high quality flows; Anthropic Claude for red-team/safety sampling.
  - Persistence: KV-cache for session history; some in-process caching for prefixes.

- Success criteria (what SaaSCo said matters):
  - Latency: P95 < 300ms for single-turn chat on typical 1k token request (target).
  - Cost: reduce per-token inference costs by ~35–50% while maintaining output quality.
  - Functional parity: support for streaming, function-calling-style structured output, and embedding compatibility.
  - Compliance: private/VPC deployment option + audit logs and KMS integration.

Model compatibility & shortlist we discussed
- Needs: OpenAI-compatible API surface (chat/completions + function-calling), tokenizer parity or easy migration path, streaming, and quantized model support for cost/latency.
- Shortlist (initial):
  - Llama 2 13B — strong instruction-following with quantization options.
  - Mistral-Instruct / Mistral 7B variants — good cost/quality ratio.
  - MPT-7B-Instruct — lightweight option for high volume flows.
  - Anthropic-compatible safety shim (we recommend keeping Anthropic for critical safety checks during pilot).

Proposed next steps (owners & timing)
1) Redwood: share evaluation plan + benchmark harness by Wed (attached: redwood-eval-plan-v1.pdf). Owner: Vanessa.
2) SaaSCo: share a 20–30 example prompt set and canonical eval rubric (quality metrics) by Fri. Owner: James / Claire.
3) Tech deep-dive: schedule 60m call (infra + security) for next week to review VPC options and KMS integration. Owner: Rishi.
4) Pilot proposal & estimate: Redwood to provide a 6-week pilot scope and cost estimate (includes dedicated quantized instance options). Owner: Vanessa.

Attachments included: saasco-discovery-notes.pdf, redwood-eval-plan-v1.pdf, SaaSCo-MAP-v1.xlsx

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the calendar invite for the technical deep-dive once James confirms availability.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: James Li <james.li@saasco.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Nguyen <claire.nguyen@saasco.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Today’s discovery — migration off OpenAI/Anthropic

Vanessa — thanks for the thorough recap, this matches our notes. A few clarifications and one ask:

- Timeline: we’d like the pilot estimate and scope in the week of 4/27 so we can align with procurement (quarter close).
- Latency: the 300ms P95 is for most interactive flows; a small subset of long-context assistant sessions can tolerate higher latency (up to 600ms). I’ll send an annotated example list.
- Function-calling: critical for our integrations with the booking service; any mismatch will require changes to our proxy. API shape parity is non-negotiable for the initial pilot.
- Security: procurement will require SOC2 evidence and an initial compliance questionnaire — can you confirm who from Redwood handles that?

We’ll share the sample prompts and rubric by Friday. Looking forward to the eval plan.

—James
James Li
Head of Platform Engineering, SaaSCo
james.li@saasco.com | +1 (650) 555-0147

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 21 Apr 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: SAA SCo discovery follow-up & preliminary ops notes

Quick internal note while I prep the deep-dive:
- Action items for eng: prepare benchmark harness that can replay their 20–30 prompt set with our quantized L2-13B and Mistral variants. Include streaming + function-calling emulation.
- Security/compliance: loop in Monica to start the SOC2 evidence pack and initial questionnaire. Monica, can you confirm lead time for the pack? Do we have any items that require legal sign-off (NDA/BAA)?
- Ops question: they run ~10M tokens/month today. For cost modelling, I’ll assume 2–4x peak multiplier for concurrency. Need to confirm their QPS spike patterns on the deep-dive.

I’ll draft the pilot SOW skeleton and share by EOD.

Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
